decision_reason: Retain the broad A1 motion concepts and refine posture with an independent lateral-orientation dimension. Lying on back and lying on right side differ only in smoothness in A1, although static torso orientation provides a more physically justified distinction. Sitting and lying on back have the lowest unseen-pair separation, but their existing inclination contrast is defensible; additional seated-joint geometry cannot be assumed from unspecified leg-sensor placement. The relatively weak seen coverage for moving around in an elevator does not justify an elevator-specific attribute. Preserve transferable motion descriptors rather than inventing reliable elevator displacement, stair direction, or treadmill-grade measurements.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: torso_lateral_inclination
attributes.definition: Magnitude of sustained sideways torso inclination relative to gravity, expressed by the absolute component of the gravity direction along the torso's anatomical left-right direction; this distinguishes lateral from sagittal inclination without encoding left versus right.

levels.Low: Little sustained lateral inclination; gravity lies approximately within the torso's sagittal plane.
levels.Medium: Moderate sustained lateral inclination; gravity has an intermediate lateral component.
levels.High: Strong sustained lateral inclination; gravity is directed approximately along the torso's left-right direction.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: motion_regularity
attributes.definition: Temporal consistency and predictability of the motion pattern.

levels.Low: Irregular and poorly predictable motion pattern.
levels.Medium: Partly structured motion with moderate variability.

operations.reason: motion_intensity: G3 supports observable acceleration and rotation magnitude across the available body sensors. This retains broad transfer from vigorous and moderate seen activities to stair locomotion and elevator movement. Effort is not equivalent to measured motion energy, and movement style can blur adjacent levels; intensity alone should not distinguish stair direction or treadmill grade.
seen_anchors: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in 15 deg inclined positions)

operations.reason: cadence: G6 supports repetition rate in recurring limb acceleration and rotation. Seen walking and running provide transferable rate contrasts for unseen walking and stairs. Irregular movement, short windows, and multiple repetitions within one movement cycle can make the meaningful unit ambiguous; no exact rate is inferred from an activity name.
target_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)
seen_anchors: running on a treadmill with a speed of 8 km/h

operations.reason: smoothness: G9 supports sustained rapid signal changes, distinguishing continuous movement from persistently fluctuating movement. This transfers across treadmill locomotion, stairs, and irregular elevator movement. Sensor attachment and movement speed can affect apparent smoothness; static lying orientations do not inherently warrant different smoothness levels.
target_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)
seen_anchors: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in 15 deg inclined positions)

operations.reason: impulsiveness: G10 supports isolated abrupt acceleration changes associated with contact and landing. Jumping provides a transferable impact anchor for descending stairs, complementing sustained smoothness rather than duplicating it. Footwear, contact strategy, sensor location, and elevator transients can alter peaks; impacts do not uniquely identify descent.
seen_anchors: running on a treadmill with a speed of 8 km/h

operations.reason: posture_inclination: Preserve its exact global-posture meaning. G1 supports mean gravity-relative orientation across torso and limbs, retaining the existing sitting-versus-lying contrast and upright-versus-recumbent transfer. Articulated seated configurations and dynamic acceleration make a single global inclination less precise. torso_lateral_inclination: G1 supports the torso's sustained lateral gravity component, providing an independent distinction between lying on back and lying on right side without relying on their questionable A1 smoothness difference. Standing supplies a low-lateral anchor and lying on right side a high-lateral anchor. Predictability is strongest during stable posture; sensor-to-anatomical alignment is required, and rolling, dynamic acceleration, or oblique reclining can create intermediate or ambiguous evidence. No particular mounting alignment is assumed to have already been established.
seen_anchors: cycling on an exercise bike in horizontal positions

operations.reason: posture_variability: G12 supports changes in gravity-relative body configuration over time. This retains a transferable contrast between stable treadmill posture and more variable whole-body movement, with rowing as a substantial-variation anchor. Local limb cycling must not be mistaken for global posture change, and brief windows may omit transitions.
target_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)
seen_anchors: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in 15 deg inclined positions)

operations.reason: rotational_motion: G2 supports angular movement measured by torso and limb gyroscopes. It offers seen-supported evidence for active movement versus stillness and preserves a distinction from linear motion. Limb swings and torso turns both contribute, so prominence does not specify a unique movement mechanism or guarantee a distinction between similar exercise machines.

translational_motion: G13 supports short-window linear-motion proxies, preserving a broad locomotion-versus-stationary-exercise concept with seen walking and cycling anchors. Predictability is limited: inertial signals do not reliably establish constant-speed transport or long-term displacement, and treadmill limb progression differs from environmental progression. Retain the concept without adding elevator travel direction, absolute elevation, or a guaranteed overground-versus-treadmill distinction.
target_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)
seen_anchors: cycling on an exercise bike in vertical positions

operations.reason: motion_regularity: G11 and G6 support recurrence and temporal consistency, independently of repetition rate. This provides a transferable bridge from structured treadmill movement and less predictable basketball movement to unseen regular locomotion and moving around in an elevator. Stillness can also be highly predictable, and brief or unusually repetitive elevator movement may obscure the expected contrast.
target_unseen: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)
seen_anchors: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in 15 deg inclined positions)

semantic_redundancy_review: The ten attributes retain complementary magnitude, rate, sustained fluctuation, transient impact, posture, angular-motion, linear-motion, and predictability concepts. Smoothness and impulsiveness distinguish sustained fluctuations from isolated peaks; cadence and regularity distinguish repetition rate from consistency. Global inclination and torso lateral inclination are not interchangeable: supine and side-lying configurations can both be globally horizontal while differing in lateral orientation. Posture variability concerns change rather than mean orientation. All activity pairs were considered, especially the one- and two-coordinate A1 neighbors. No additional distinction is imposed on stepper versus cross trainer, the two cycling positions, or flat versus inclined treadmill walking because handle use, precise joint geometry, and stable grade-specific kinematics are not established by the supplied semantics. Sitting versus lying on back retains its existing global-posture contrast rather than adding an unreliable leg-placement-dependent attribute. These are feasibility judgments, not measured separability or prediction performance.
